prompt:
Public specification:
For each bit in a 32-bit vector, capture when the input signal changes from 1 in one clock cycle to 0 the next. "Capture" means that the output will remain 1 until the register is reset (active high synchronous reset).

Input widths {'reset': 1, 'in': 32}; output widths {'out': 32}. Clock clk; sample after the posedge edge has settled. Each row's values are driven before the sampled edge. Optional mid input changes occur AFTER sampling, before the other edge, and are carried to the start of the next row. Protocol seed 20261121.
Respond to EVERY supplied issue in order with compact JSON {responses:[
{issue_id,decision:"accept"|"rebut",reason,spec_quote,edits:[{path:[strings],value}]}]}.
For rebut, use an exact spec quotation and no edits. Use rebut when the contract already has the
proposed value or its existing example already expresses the rule. Compare against Current contract
before writing an edit. A rebuttal quote must come from Public specification. Port widths and
experiment timing instructions supplied after it are not spec quotes. An accept must change a field. Prefer
a small edit such as
["rules","rule_ID","condition"], ["states","state_name","meaning"], or ["reset","first_released_cycle"].
Whole fields may also be replaced as ["rules","rule_ID"], ["states"], ["reset"], ["mid"], ["uncertain"].
A whole rule may add or delete by id (delete with null). Preserve the current schema, including reset
kind none, sync, async or unspecified, reset name a public input or null, and exact same_cycle /
next_cycle strings. Put initial-value clarification without a physical reset in state meaning or an
explicit uncertain field rather than making up a reset kind. EVERY rule example remains 2–4 cycles.
If changing uncertain, preserve its shape: [{rule_id (existing rule or "global"),note,candidates:
[one or more distinct strings giving plausible interpretations]}].
Include all issue responses in order, including those unchanged from any previous attempt. No port changes.
